newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Britain wants EU message to China on HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Britain wants EU message to China on HK handover.

text.p: Britain said on Thursday it was not seeking a European Union boycott of the swearing-in ceremony for a Beijing-picked legislature in Hong Kong but that it wanted a clear message to China to respect the handover agreement.

Arriving for a meeting with fellow foreign ministers, Britain's Robin Cook told reporters he wanted the 15-nation bloc to issue a statement urging Beijing to stick to its word once the colony reverts to China in four days time.
"We want to make sure that Hong Kong can boast a prosperous economy and also maintain its freedoms and liberties," Cook said.
British officials sharply rejected media reports that London was planning to make a last-minute plea to its EU partners to keep their ministers away from the swearing-in ceremony.
Most EU countries plan a ministerial presence at the event.
To the fury of Hong Kong democrats, Britain and the United States both appeared to be easing their stance on Thursday, planning to send top officials to the ceremony.

Cook denied that Britain was taking a new position and rejected accusations that Europe was sending China a mixed message by having British ministers boycott the ceremony while their EU compatriots were present.
"It is entirely right that Britain should signal its own political concern on this issue," he said.

Cook said the important thing was for China to meet its obligations under the agreement leading to the handover. If there were any backtracking, he said, London would seek international support for a response.
